text:
Mavrik Bourque arrived in Nashville on July 1 in a trade with Dallas (alongside Ilya Lyubushkin) and signed a six-year, $33 million deal days later, per ESPN. Fifteen games in, he's still looking for his first goal as a Predator, and Predlines summed up the mood: "Predators are still waiting for Mavrik Bourque to break out."

Our numbers say the drought is more bad luck than lost touch. He has zero goals on 3.8 expected and 31 shots, and his rate of quality chances (0.94 expected goals per 60) is higher than last season, when he scored 20 for the Stars. In Tuesday's shutout in Los Angeles he had five shots worth 0.78 expected goals and nothing to show for it. The harder issue is the other end: at five-on-five, Nashville's share of expected goals is nine points worse with him on the ice than without. His style is distinct, too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups coming from behind the net (8% for a typical forward), the kind of pass that makes goalies turn and search. The team has won six straight around him; the first goal would help everyone relax.
headline: Mavrik Bourque is still waiting on goal one
